children: There's been no V-shaped recovery for the market this time
The S&P 500 has become stuck below an important trendline.
Another slide for stock futures early Wednesday makes an unwelcome metric for Wall Street very likely.

"Bulls don't want to see this," said Bluekurtic Market Insights in a post on X, as the firm noted that the S&P 500 is in danger of closing below its 50-day moving average for the second week in a row.

Investors of a technical bent use moving averages as simplified indicators of an asset's price trend. The 50-day and 200-day moving averages are particularly popular as medium and longer-term trends, often providing support off which a price can bounce.
However, should an asset price drop below the moving averages on a sustained basis then what was support can turn into a ceiling, up against which rallies are more readily rebuffed.

The S&P 500's stalling for several months, followed by a sharp retreat in the past few weeks, caused Wall Street's main stock barometer to drop through its 50-DMA at the end of October. A subsequent bounce failed against the trendline, and a further retreat has followed.
This action stands in contrast to the market's tendency over many years to enjoy a V-shaped recovery as stoic investors buy the dip.
Bluekurtic ran the numbers for what tends to happen next should the V-shape recovery not swiftly occur and the S&P 500 SPX stays below the 50-DMA for at least two consecutive weeks.
"In 17 of 18 prior cases, $SPX fell further at some point within next month. By 3 months, it fell 100% of the time with 5.6% median loss," the research service said.
